rundown: France beat South Africa 21-19 at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, Reunion. France led 21-19 at the half and held on.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 13, 3:06 PM ET. It had South Africa 51% and France 49%, projecting South Africa 30.8 – France 30.3 (61 total, South Africa by 0.5).

Final: South Africa 19 – France 21. Wrong winner: it had South Africa at 51%, and France (49%) won.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
South Africa came in with a 39% above average attack and a 20% stingier than average defense (WLWWW, 49 scored and 14 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 11 and 11 games of evidence. Projected to score 30.8, they scored 19 (−11.8 points, 38% under); projected to allow 30.3, they allowed 21 (−9.3 points, 31% under).

France came in with a 35% above average attack and a 7% stingier than average defense (WWWLW, 42.5 scored and 23 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 11 and 11 games of evidence. Projected to score 30.3, they scored 21 (−9.3 points, 31% under); projected to allow 30.8, they allowed 19 (−11.8 points, 38% under).

The bigger miss was South Africa's scoring (-11.8 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 40 against 61 projected (-21), about the 8th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15).

Margin: France by 2 against South Africa by 0.5 projected, about the 56th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±16).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; there were no odds to check the projection against.

The result was off its normal range without being an outlier, so the flags may have played a part.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.658 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +2.5 points. It counts toward Rugby scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Rugby learning switches on at 20 graded games (14 so far).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
